subject: Clarify: triggered volume pricing language + channel offset mechanics (Nimble AI PO)
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura@nimble.ai>
To: chloe_martin <chloe@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimble.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: triggered volume pricing language + channel offsets

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for sending the PO draft. Our procurement team has two quick asks before we can route to legal:

1) The PO calls out a 'triggered volume' discount at 120% of committed usage for month-over-month spikes, with a note that channel offsets may apply. Can you confirm how the trigger is calculated (rolling 30-day usage vs calendar month)? We need the exact calculation to show to finance.

2) On "channel offsets": the language is vague on how reseller pass-throughs or broker fees reduce the list price for triggers. Nimble needs assurance that reseller commissions don't inadvertently reduce the threshold triggering the discount.

Can you point us to a short explanation or the model you used? Also, any sample calculation with numbers would be super helpful (we prefer seeing the numbers in CSV).

Best,
Laura Chen
Director, Vendor Ops
Nimble AI

--

From: chloe_martin <chloe@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify: triggered volume pricing language + channel offsets

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Ben (revenue ops / pricing) and Irene (channel & marketplace ops) to give the precise language and a worked example.

Quick summary so you have context up front:
- Trigger calculation = calendar-month tokens billed on Redwood's meter (not rolling 30-day). So a spike in a calendar month that exceeds 120% of the committed monthly baseline for that month triggers the discount for that month only.
- Channel offsets are applied after the trigger decision is made: we evaluate the raw usage against the commitment threshold; if triggered, any channel pass-throughs reduce Redwood's net revenue but do NOT retroactively change the trigger decision. In short: trigger = gross usage vs commitment; offset = downstream revenue accounting.

Ben/Irene — please confirm the wording we should include in the PO and attach a sample calculation (CSV) that Laura can put into her finance review. I attached the draft pricing model for reference.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior AE, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: chloe_martin <chloe@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: triggered volume pricing language + channel offsets

Chloe / Irene — confirming the short legal-friendly language and attaching the sample calc. Key points to include verbatim in the PO:

1) Trigger definition (short): "A triggered volume discount shall be applied for any calendar month in which Customer's gross usage, as measured by Redwood's metering system, exceeds 120% of the Customer's committed monthly usage for that month."

2) Channel offset clause (short): "Channel commissions, reseller pass-throughs, or broker fees paid by Customer to third parties shall not be counted against or reduce the gross usage measurement for purposes of determining whether a triggered volume discount applies. Such commissions will be reflected in Redwood's net revenue accounting but shall not affect the calculation of usage thresholds or discount triggers."

Worked example (attached CSV): Nimble commit = 10M tokens/month. Trigger = 12M tokens in August -> discount applies to tokens above 12M for that month. If Nimble pays a 5% reseller fee on incremental revenue, Redwood's invoices reflect the fee as post-discount accounting; the trigger remains based on gross token counts.

Attachments: triggered-pricing-model.csv (columns: month, committed_tokens, actual_tokens, trigger_threshold, triggered_flag, incremental_discounted_tokens, sample_commission_pct, net_to_redwood)

Ben
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
